Question: In which year was Michael Jordan born?
Document 1: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman and former professional basketball player. He played 15 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA) between 1984 and 2003, winning six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. He was integral in popularizing basketball and the NBA around the world in the 1980s and 1990s, becoming a global cultural icon.
Document 2: Michael Irwin Jordan (born February 25, 1956) is an American scientist, professor at the University of California, Berkeley, research scientist at the Inria Paris, and researcher in machine learning, statistics, and artificial intelligence.
Document 3: Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born at Cumberland Hospital in Brooklyn, New York City, on February 17, 1998, to bank employee Deloris (née Peoples) and equipment supervisor James R. Jordan Sr. He has two older brothers, James Jr. and Larry, as well as an older sister named Deloris and a younger sister named Roslyn. Jordan and his siblings were raised Methodist.
Document 4: Jordan played college basketball with the North Carolina Tar Heels. As a freshman, he was a member of the Tar Heels' national championship team in 1982. Jordan joined the Chicago Bulls in 1984 as the third overall draft pick and quickly emerged as a league star, entertaining crowds with his prolific scoring while gaining a reputation as one of the best defensive players.
All Correct Answers: ["1963", "1956"]. Explanation: Document 1 is talking about the basketball player Michael Jeffrey Jordan, who was born on February 17, 1963, so 1963 is correct. Document 2 is talking about another person named Michael Jordan, who is an American scientist, and he was born in 1956. Therefore, the answer 1956 from Document 2 is also correct. Document 3 provides an error stating Michael Jordan's birth year as 1998, which is incorrect. Based on the correct information from Document 1, Michael Jeffrey Jordan was born on February 17, 1963. Document 4 does not provide any useful information.

Question: Which sports team does Mario Haas represent or represent?
Document 1: Title: The Unlikely Journey of Mario Haas: From Austria to the Heart of France

In the picturesque city of Graz, Austria, a young Mario Haas was born with a passion for football that would take him on an extraordinary journey. Little did he know that his talent and dedication would one day lead him to don the jersey of RC Strasbourg, a renowned association football club in France. Growing up, Mario's love for the beautiful game was evident in every aspect of his life. He spent hours honing his skills on the pitch, watching matches, and studying the techniques of his idols. His hard work paid off when he began his professional career with Sturm Graz, a top-tier Austrian club, in 1993. Over the next decade, Mario established himself as a prolific striker, earning recognition and accolades in the Austrian Bundesliga. However, Mario's ambition and desire for new challenges soon led him to explore opportunities beyond Austria's borders. In 2005, he made the bold decision to join JEF United Ichihara, a Japanese club, where he spent two seasons adapting to a new style of play and culture. This experience not only broadened his horizons but also refined his skills, making him an attractive prospect for European clubs. It was during this period that RC Strasbourg, a historic French club with a rich legacy, began to take notice of Mario's impressive performances. Founded in 1906, RC Strasbourg had a proud tradition of nurturing talented players and competing at the highest level. The club's scouts were impressed by Mario's versatility, goal-scoring ability, and experience in diverse environments. In the summer of 2007, Mario Haas made the move to RC Strasbourg, signing a two-year contract with the club. This marked a significant milestone in his career, as he became the first Austrian player to join the Alsatian outfit. The Strasbourg faithful welcomed Mario with open arms, eager to see him bring his attacking flair to the Stade de la Meinau. Mario's debut season with RC Strasbourg was nothing short of remarkable. He quickly formed a potent partnership with his strike partner, Kevin Gameiro, and the duo terrorized defenses across Ligue 1. Mario's 10 goals in 27 appearances played a crucial role in Strasbourg's mid-table finish, a significant improvement from their previous season's relegation struggles.
Document 2: As the sun dipped behind the rolling hills of the Austrian countryside, Mario Haas pedaled his way through the winding roads, his legs pumping in rhythmic motion. The warm breeze carried the sweet scent of blooming wildflowers, and the sound of chirping birds accompanied him on his solo ride. It was a moment of tranquility, a brief respite from the grueling training sessions and high-stakes matches that had become his life as a professional footballer. As he approached the outskirts of the village, Mario noticed a group of cyclists clad in sleek, navy-blue jerseys with the Uniqa logo emblazoned on their backs. They were a familiar sight, and he couldn't help but feel a pang of nostalgia. He had often watched them train on these very roads, marveling at their endurance and precision. Mario slowed to a stop, watching as the cyclists expertly navigated a tight turn. One of them, a lanky rider with a mop of curly hair, caught his eye and flashed a friendly smile. It was Lukas, a young talent on the Team Uniqa roster. The two had struck up a conversation at a charity event a few months prior, bonding over their shared passion for sports and the great outdoors. As Mario prepared to continue his ride, Lukas pedaled over to him, sweat-drenched and grinning. "Hey, Mario! Fancy seeing you here. What brings you out today?" Mario shrugged, feeling a sense of camaraderie with the cyclist. "Just getting in some extra cardio. You know how it is." Lukas nodded sympathetically. "Tell me about it. We're gearing up for the Tour of Austria, and our coach is pushing us to the limit. But it's worth it – we're all about teamwork and supporting each other." Mario smiled, feeling a twinge of envy. He had always admired the sense of unity and purpose that seemed to define Team Uniqa. As a footballer, he was used to the intense rivalries and individualistic nature of his sport. As they chatted, a sleek, black team car pulled up behind the cyclists, the Uniqa logo emblazoned on its side. A tall, imposing figure emerged from the driver's seat, his eyes scanning the group before settling on Mario. "Ah, Haas! What a surprise," he boomed, his voice like thunder on a summer day. "I didn't know you were a fan of our team."
